title.en: Discourse Markers (furthermore, albeit, owing to, in other words)
title.es: Los marcadores del discurso (furthermore, albeit, owing to, in other words)

text.en: Discourse markers link ideas in a longer text: they add (furthermore), concede (albeit, admittedly), give a cause (owing to), clarify (in other words) and close (in conclusion). At C1 level but, and and because are not enough: polished text uses more exact markers. The Spanish “además”, “es decir”, “debido a” and “en conclusión” match them, but the English markers have a fixed place and punctuation (a comma).
text.es: Los marcadores del discurso unen ideas en un texto más largo: añaden (furthermore), conceden (albeit, admittedly), dan una causa (owing to), aclaran (in other words) y cierran (in conclusion). En el nivel C1 no bastan but, and y because: un texto cuidado usa marcadores más exactos. El «además», el «es decir», el «debido a» y el «en conclusión» del español les corresponden, pero los marcadores del inglés tienen un lugar y una puntuación fijos (una coma).

rows: aunque (+ adjetivo o frase breve, formal)

text.en: These add a new point to the previous one. They stand at the start of a new sentence, with a comma: “The plan is cheap. Furthermore, it is easy to carry out.” After in addition to comes a noun or an -ing form.
text.es: Estos añaden un argumento nuevo al anterior. Van al inicio de una oración nueva, con coma: «The plan is cheap. Furthermore, it is easy to carry out.» Después de in addition to va un sustantivo o una forma -ing.

examples.es: The plan is cheap. Furthermore, it is easy to carry out.

tr.en: The plan is cheap. Furthermore, it is easy to carry out.
tr.es: El plan es barato. Además, es fácil de ejecutar.

examples.es: In addition, the service is excellent.

tr.en: In addition, the service is excellent.
tr.es: Además, el servicio es excelente.

text.en: Admittedly admits a weakness. Albeit is a short, formal “although”: an adjective or a short phrase follows, not a full clause. Notwithstanding + noun is a very formal “despite”.
text.es: Admittedly reconoce una debilidad. Albeit es un «aunque» corto y formal: le sigue un adjetivo o una frase corta, no una oración completa. Notwithstanding + sustantivo es un «a pesar de» muy formal.

examples.es: The test was successful, albeit limited.

tr.en: The test was successful, albeit limited.
tr.es: La prueba fue exitosa, aunque limitada.

examples.es: Notwithstanding the rain, the match went ahead.

tr.en: Notwithstanding the rain, the match went ahead.
tr.es: A pesar de la lluvia, el partido se llevó a cabo.

title.en: Cause with a noun: owing to, due to, in view of, on account of
title.es: Causa con sustantivo: owing to, due to, in view of, on account of

text.en: A noun phrase follows these, not a clause: “Owing to the traffic, we arrived late.” Before a clause you need because, since or as.
text.es: Después de estos va un grupo nominal, no una oración: «Owing to the traffic, we arrived late.» Antes de una oración hace falta because, since o as.

examples.es: Owing to the traffic, we arrived late.

tr.en: Owing to the traffic, we arrived late.
tr.es: Debido al tráfico, llegamos tarde.

examples.es: We canceled the trip in view of the weather.

tr.en: We canceled the trip in view of the weather.
tr.es: Cancelamos el viaje en vista del clima.

title.en: Clarifying and examples: in other words, namely, such as
title.es: Aclarar y ejemplificar: in other words, namely, such as

text.en: In other words and that is to say say the same thing differently. Namely lists by name. Such as gives an example, and for instance stands at the start of a sentence.
text.es: In other words y that is to say dicen lo mismo de otra manera. Namely enumera por nombre. Such as da un ejemplo, y for instance va al inicio de una oración.

examples.es: The results were inconclusive. In other words, we need more data.

tr.en: The results were inconclusive. In other words, we need more data.
tr.es: Los resultados no fueron concluyentes. Es decir, necesitamos más datos.

examples.es: Some animals, such as elephants, live in groups.

tr.en: Some animals, such as elephants, live in groups.
tr.es: Algunos animales, como los elefantes, viven en grupos.

title.en: Order and closing: firstly, subsequently, in conclusion
title.es: Orden y cierre: firstly, subsequently, in conclusion

text.en: Firstly, secondly, subsequently, finally mark the order. For closing: in conclusion, to sum up, overall, above all (especially).
text.es: Firstly, secondly, subsequently, finally marcan el orden. Para cerrar: in conclusion, to sum up, overall, above all (sobre todo).

examples.es: In conclusion, the results were positive.

tr.en: In conclusion, the results were positive.
tr.es: En conclusión, los resultados fueron positivos.

examples.es: Above all, the project was a success.

tr.en: Above all, the project was a success.
tr.es: Sobre todo, el proyecto fue un éxito.

text.en: A comma follows the marker: “Furthermore, it is cheap.” After albeit there is no full clause (subject and verb), only an adjective or a short phrase. Before a full clause you need although.
text.es: Después del marcador va una coma: «Furthermore, it is cheap.» Después de albeit no va una oración completa (sujeto y verbo), solo un adjetivo o una frase corta. Antes de una oración completa hace falta although.

text.en: After owing to and due to comes a noun, not a clause: not “owing to we were late”, but “owing to the traffic” or “because we were late”.
text.es: Después de owing to y due to va un sustantivo, no una oración: no «owing to we were late», sino «owing to the traffic» o «because we were late».

speak.en: Discourse markers link ideas in a longer text. «Furthermore», «moreover» and «in addition» add. «Admittedly», «albeit» and «notwithstanding» express a concession: «The test was successful, albeit limited». A cause with a noun is given by «owing to» and «in view of»: «Owing to the traffic, we arrived late». «In other words» and «namely» clarify. «In conclusion» and «to sum up» close. A comma follows the marker.
speak.es: Los marcadores del discurso unen ideas en un texto más largo. «Furthermore», «moreover» e «in addition» añaden. «Admittedly», «albeit» y «notwithstanding» expresan una concesión: «The test was successful, albeit limited». Una causa con sustantivo la dan «owing to» e «in view of»: «Owing to the traffic, we arrived late». «In other words» y «namely» aclaran. «In conclusion» y «to sum up» cierran. Después del marcador va una coma.

gloss.en: but, in spite of the fact

items.sentence: The plan is cheap. ___, it is easy to carry out.

Although.en: Although marks a contrast and introduces a clause, with no comma after it.
Although.es: Although marca un contraste e introduce una cláusula, sin coma después.

Despite.en: After despite comes a noun or an -ing form, not a comma.
Despite.es: Después de despite va un sustantivo o una forma -ing, no una coma.

examples: It is cheap. Furthermore, it is fast.
She is kind. Furthermore, she is funny.

tr.en: The plan is cheap. Furthermore, it is easy to carry out.
tr.es: El plan es barato. Además, es fácil de llevar a cabo.

items.sentence: The hotel is clean and, ___, very cheap.

why.en: An addition inside a sentence: and, moreover, very cheap.
why.es: Una adición dentro de la oración: and, moreover, very cheap.

otherwise.en: Otherwise means a consequence or “if not”; here an addition is needed.
otherwise.es: Otherwise significa una consecuencia o «si no»; aquí hace falta una adición.

whereas.en: Whereas sets two facts against each other; here an addition is needed.
whereas.es: Whereas contrapone dos hechos; aquí hace falta una adición.

examples: It is good and, moreover, cheap.
He is smart and, moreover, kind.

tr.en: The hotel is clean and, moreover, very cheap.
tr.es: El hotel está limpio y, además, muy barato.

items.sentence: ___ the rain, the match went ahead.

why.en: A very formal “despite” before a noun: Notwithstanding the rain.
why.es: Un «a pesar de» muy formal antes de un sustantivo: Notwithstanding the rain.

Although.en: After Although you need a clause (although it rained), not a noun.
Although.es: Después de Although hace falta una cláusula (although it rained), no un sustantivo.

Because.en: After Because you need a clause, and it marks a cause, not a contrast.
Because.es: Después de Because hace falta una cláusula, y marca una causa, no un contraste.

examples: Notwithstanding the cost, we bought it.

tr.en: Notwithstanding the rain, the match went ahead.
tr.es: A pesar de la lluvia, el partido se llevó a cabo.

why.en: A short formal “although” before an adjective: albeit limited.
why.es: Un «aunque» corto y formal antes de un adjetivo: albeit limited.

despite.en: After despite you need a noun, not an adjective (limited).
despite.es: Después de despite hace falta un sustantivo, no un adjetivo (limited).

whereas.en: After whereas you need a clause, not an adjective.
whereas.es: Después de whereas hace falta una cláusula, no un adjetivo.

tr.en: The test was successful, albeit limited.
tr.es: La prueba fue exitosa, aunque limitada.

items.sentence: ___ to the heavy traffic, we arrived late.

why.en: A cause with a noun: Owing to + noun phrase.
why.es: Una causa con sustantivo: Owing to + grupo nominal.

Owed.en: Owed to is the participle of the verb “owe”; you need Owing.
Owed.es: Owed to es el participio del verbo «deber»; hace falta Owing.

Own.en: “Own to” does not exist in this meaning; you need Owing to.
Own.es: «Own to» no existe en este sentido; hace falta Owing to.

examples: Owing to the rain, we left.

tr.en: Owing to the heavy traffic, we arrived late.
tr.es: Debido al tráfico pesado, llegamos tarde.

items.sentence: We canceled the trip ___ view of the weather.

why.en: A fixed phrase: in view of.
why.es: Una expresión fija: in view of.

on.en: “On view of” does not exist; you need in view of.
on.es: «On view of» no existe; hace falta in view of.

at.en: “At view of” does not exist; you need in view of.
at.es: «At view of» no existe; hace falta in view of.

examples: In view of the facts, we agree.
In view of this, we stop.

tr.en: We canceled the trip in view of the weather.
tr.es: Cancelamos el viaje en vista del clima.

items.sentence: ___, the service was slow, but the food was excellent.

Admitted.en: Admitted is a participle; the sentence-opening adverb is Admittedly.
Admitted.es: Admitted es un participio; el adverbio al inicio de la oración es Admittedly.

Admitting.en: Admitting is an -ing form; the sentence-opening adverb is Admittedly.
Admitting.es: Admitting es una forma -ing; el adverbio al inicio de la oración es Admittedly.

tr.en: Admittedly, the service was slow, but the food was excellent.
tr.es: Es cierto que el servicio fue lento, pero la comida estaba excelente.

items.sentence: The service is excellent. ___, the prices are reasonable.

why.en: An addition at the start of a sentence: In addition,
why.es: Una adición al inicio de la oración: In addition,

In addition to.en: After in addition to you need a noun, not a comma.
In addition to.es: Después de in addition to hace falta un sustantivo, no una coma.

Addition.en: Addition alone is not a marker; you need In addition.
Addition.es: Addition solo no es un marcador; hace falta In addition.

tr.en: The service is excellent. In addition, the prices are reasonable.
tr.es: El servicio es excelente. Además, los precios son razonables.

items.sentence: The results were inconclusive. ___, we need more data.

Other words.en: Other words alone is not a marker; you need In other words.
Other words.es: Other words solo no es un marcador; hace falta In other words.

On other words.en: “On other words” does not exist; you need In other words.
On other words.es: «On other words» no existe; hace falta In other words.

tr.en: The results were inconclusive. In other words, we need more data.
tr.es: Los resultados no fueron concluyentes. En otras palabras, necesitamos más datos.

items.sentence: Several countries, ___ France and Spain, joined the plan.

nameable.en: Nameable is an adjective (“able to be named”); you need namely.
nameable.es: Nameable es un adjetivo («que se puede nombrar»); hace falta namely.

names.en: Names is a noun or a verb; you need namely.
names.es: Names es un sustantivo o un verbo; hace falta namely.

examples: Two men, namely Tom and Sam, left.
Three cities, namely Rome, Paris and Lima.

tr.en: Several countries, namely France and Spain, joined the plan.
tr.es: Varios países, concretamente Francia y España, se unieron al plan.

items.sentence: Some animals, ___ elephants, live in groups.

as such.en: As such means “in itself”; for an example you need such as.
as such.es: As such significa «en sí mismo»; para un ejemplo hace falta such as.

such like.en: “Such like” is not the usual example phrase; you need such as.
such like.es: «Such like» no es la expresión habitual de ejemplo; hace falta such as.

examples: Fruits, such as apples, are cheap.
Cities such as Rome are old.

tr.en: Some animals, such as elephants, live in groups.
tr.es: Algunos animales, como los elefantes, viven en grupos.

items.sentence: ___ all, the project was a success.

why.en: A fixed phrase: above all (most of all).
why.es: Una expresión fija: above all (sobre todo).

Over.en: “Over all” is not the usual phrase; you need Above all or Overall.
Over.es: «Over all» no es la expresión habitual; hace falta Above all u Overall.

On.en: “On all” does not exist in this meaning; you need Above all.
On.es: «On all» no existe en este sentido; hace falta Above all.

tr.en: Above all, the project was a success.
tr.es: Sobre todo, el proyecto fue un éxito.

items.sentence: ___ sum up, the plan has three main advantages.

For.en: “For sum up” does not exist; you need To sum up.
For.es: «For sum up» no existe; hace falta To sum up.

In.en: “In sum up” does not exist; you need To sum up or In sum.
In.es: «In sum up» no existe; hace falta To sum up o In sum.

tr.en: To sum up, the plan has three main advantages.
tr.es: En resumen, el plan tiene tres ventajas principales.

concluding.en: “In concluding” is not the usual marker; you need In conclusion.
concluding.es: «In concluding» no es el marcador habitual; hace falta In conclusion.

concluded.en: “In concluded” is not correct; you need a noun (conclusion).
concluded.es: «In concluded» no es correcto; hace falta un sustantivo (conclusion).

tr.en: In conclusion, the results were positive.
tr.es: En conclusión, los resultados fueron positivos.

items.sentence: ___, we will review the budget; subsequently, we will decide.

First of.en: “First of” alone is incomplete; it would need First of all.
First of.es: «First of» solo está incompleto; necesitaría First of all.

Firstly of.en: “Firstly of” does not exist; you need Firstly or First of all.
Firstly of.es: «Firstly of» no existe; hace falta Firstly o First of all.

tr.en: Firstly, we will review the budget; subsequently, we will decide.
tr.es: Primero revisaremos el presupuesto; posteriormente, decidiremos.

items.sentence: She missed the meeting ___ a result of illness.

why.en: A cause with a noun: as a result of.
why.es: Una causa con sustantivo: as a result of.

in.en: “In a result of” does not exist; you need as a result of.
in.es: «In a result of» no existe; hace falta as a result of.

by.en: “By a result of” does not exist; you need as a result of.
by.es: «By a result of» no existe; hace falta as a result of.

examples: As a result of the storm, we left.
He fell as a result of ice.

tr.en: She missed the meeting as a result of illness.
tr.es: Ella faltó a la reunión a causa de una enfermedad.

items.sentence: The decision was made ___ account of the cost.

why.en: A formal cause: on account of + noun.
why.es: Una causa formal: on account of + sustantivo.

in.en: “In account of” does not exist in this meaning; you need on account of.
in.es: «In account of» no existe en este sentido; hace falta on account of.

for.en: “For account of” does not exist; you need on account of.
for.es: «For account of» no existe; hace falta on account of.

examples: On account of illness, he left.
On account of the cost, no.

tr.en: The decision was made on account of the cost.
tr.es: La decisión se tomó por el costo.
